text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Elevated 5xx/504 rates detected in atl1 (Atlantic gateway). Error rate spiked to ~12% over last 5m. Pager -> oncall @ryan-oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gateway-5xx

leah: ack. seeing alerts in grafana too. joining bridge. :phone:

omar: joining. I can pull gateway and mlworker logs. allocating 2m

ryan-oncall: i'm oncall. hopping on bridge now — https://meet.redwood.com/atl1-ops

jules-sre: quick checks: gateway latency and backend 502s. running `kubectl get pods -n gateway -l region=atl1` then `kubectl top pod` to see CPU

jules-sre: output snippet:
```
pod/gateway-1   120m CPU  350Mi
pod/gateway-2   110m CPU  340Mi
pod/gateway-3   450m CPU  1.1Gi  <-- spike
```

omar: tailing logs shows repeated upstream 502s from mlworker pool-23. sample:
```
[2026-02-20T14:03:12Z] upstream(mlworker-23): 502 Bad Gateway - kvcache eviction overflow
[2026-02-20T14:03:12Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-r1 latency_ms=28
```

leah: support is reporting customer errors. mike, any big names flagged?

mike-support: yes — Acme Analytics and FinCo seeing higher error rates and timeouts on batch endpoints. CS has tickets open. pushing a temporary workaround to avoid hitting large batches.

anna-pm: do we need a customer-facing status? I can draft one for status.redwood.ai. Recommend "partial outage in Atlantic region affecting inference requests; failover in progress." 

ryan-oncall: mitigation plan:
- shift 50% new traffic from atl1 -> eu1
- enable circuit-breaker on heavy batch endpoints
- drain problematic mlworker pool-23
- monitor error-rate & latency

leah: set to start shifting now. running command:
```
redwood route update --region atl1 --weight 0.5 --fallback eu1 --dry-run=false
> ok: traffic steer started (trace: tx-179123)
```

omar: draining pool-23:
```
kubectl annotate deployment mlworker pool=pool-23 drain=true --namespace=ml
> annotated
```

omar: logs show kvcache GC thrash when batch size > 512 tokens. probable root: recent quantized kernel rollout on mlworker-23.

jules-sre: can we rollback that kernel on pool-23? if it's service-managed, we can pin to previous image for that pool.

ryan-oncall: rolling back that pool now. command:
```
kubectl set image deployment/mlworker mlworker=registry.redwood/mlworker:v1.9.1 --namespace=ml --selector=pool=pool-23
> rollout started
```

incident-bot: UPDATE: Traffic steer to eu1 active. Observed drop in 5xx from 12% -> 6% within 2m after steer. Next check in 5m.

mike-support: confirming customer reports: Acme errors reduced but still seeing intermittent 504s on long-poll batch jobs. they're asking for ETA.

anna-pm: ETA to stabilise? if rollback completes and drain finishes, we should see steady state in ~15-20m. i'll post a short update to status page now.

leah: enabling circuit-breaker threshold on batch route to reject > 400 concurrent tokens to reduce pressure:
```
redwood policy set circuit-breaker --route /v1/batch --max-inflight 400 --region atl1
> applied
```

omar: rollback completed for pool-23. new logs:
```
[2026-02-20T14:12:31Z] mlworker-23: kernel v1.9.1 restored
[2026-02-20T14:12:32Z] upstream health ok
```

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: 5xx rate in atl1 down to 2.1% over last 5m. Latency stable. Continuing to monitor for 30m before full traffic restoration.

ryan-oncall: good. hold on rollback verification: keeping traffic split 50/50 for now. anyone see residual cascading errors?

mike-support: customers are happy with reduction. CS requests a short note for impacted customers outlining cause (kernel rollout -> kvcache GC) and mitigation (rollback + steer).

anna-pm: drafting customer note. will include timeline and apology. /cc @legal if needed.

jules-sre: action items for postmortem:
- RCA: kernel change + kvcache GC interaction
- Improve rollout canary thresholds for kvcache-sensitive kernels
- Add autoscale policy to avoid single-pool CPU spike
- Add alert for kvcache eviction rate

ryan-oncall: assigning postmortem owner: leah. timeline: initial draft in 24h, final in 72h. tagging oncall handoff to tilly at 18:00 UTC.

leah: acknowledged. drafting now. will include command snippets and customer impact summary.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVE CHECK: errors under threshold for 20m. Recommend: keep traffic split for 30m then gradually restore. Close thread when done.

ryan-oncall: thanks team. handing off to tilly for follow-up during next shift. off-bridge in 2.

tilly: ack, thanks — will monitor the scheduled checks. please DM if anything else pops up.

leah: closing thread notes: mitigation successful, rollback + steer reduced errors to baseline. postmortem owner: leah. customer comm draft in progress.
